metadata.description: Plant disease classes for YOLOv8 detection model with treatment guidance

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown lesions on leaves and fruit. Leaves may curl and drop. Fruit develops scabby, corky patches.
Apple___Apple_scab.favorable_conditions: Cool, wet spring weather (15–20°C), high humidity
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_treatment: Apply neem oil spray (5ml/L water) every 7–10 days. Remove and destroy fallen leaves. Use copper-based fungicide.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L water. Captan 50% WP @ 2g/L. Apply at bud break and repeat every 10–14 days.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Prune for air circulation. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Apple___Apple_scab.economic_impact: Can reduce yield by 50–70% if untreated

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular lesions on fruit that enlarge and turn black. Leaves show frog-eye spots (purple to brown). Cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.favorable_conditions: Warm, humid weather; wounds from insects or hail
Apple___Black_rot.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected fruit and pruned branches. Apply copper fungicide. Maintain tree vigour with balanced fertilization.
Apple___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP @ 1g/L. Captan 50% WP @ 2g/L. Apply every 10–14 days during growing season.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out dead wood. Control fire blight. Remove mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.economic_impact: Significant fruit loss; can cause complete crop failure in severe cases

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface. Tube-like structures on leaf undersides. Distorted fruit.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.favorable_conditions: Wet spring weather; presence of cedar/juniper trees nearby
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.organic_treatment: Remove nearby cedar/juniper trees if possible. Apply sulfur-based sprays preventively.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil (Nova) @ 0.5ml/L. Propiconazole @ 1ml/L. Apply from pink bud stage.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Remove alternate hosts (cedar/juniper).

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms. Leaves are green and vibrant.
Apple___healthy.organic_treatment: Continue regular monitoring and good agricultural practices.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil health, proper irrigation, and balanced fertilization.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown concentric ring spots on older lower leaves (bull's-eye pattern). Yellow halo around spots. Lesions on stem and fruit.
Tomato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm days (24–29°C), cool nights, high humidity, leaf wetness
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Neem oil @ 3ml/L weekly. Remove infected leaves. Compost tea spray. Ensure plant spacing for air flow.
Tomato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L. Chlorothalonil @ 2g/L. Azoxystrobin @ 1ml/L. Apply preventively every 7–10 days.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation (3 years). Stake plants. Avoid overhead watering. Use disease-free seeds.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked grey-green lesions on leaves that turn brown. White mold on leaf undersides in humid conditions. Brown fruit rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Cool (10–20°C), wet, humid weather; foggy conditions
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy affected plants immediately. Copper-based fungicide (Bordeaux mixture). Improve drainage.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb @ 2.5g/L. Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g/L. Apply every 5–7 days during outbreaks.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified blight-resistant varieties. Avoid excessive nitrogen. Destroy infected crop debris.
Tomato___Late_blight.economic_impact: Can cause complete crop loss within 2 weeks if unchecked

Tomato___Leaf_Miner.symptoms: Winding white trails (mines) on leaf surface. Leaves turn yellow and dry. Reduced photosynthesis.
Tomato___Leaf_Miner.cause: Insect pest Tuta absoluta / Liriomyza species
Tomato___Leaf_Miner.organic_treatment: Yellow sticky traps. Neem oil spray @ 5ml/L. Release natural enemies (Diglyphus isaea).
Tomato___Leaf_Miner.prevention: Use insect-proof netting. Remove affected leaves. Monitor with sticky traps.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms. Deep green leaves, firm fruit.
Tomato___healthy.organic_treatment: Continue current practices. Regular monitoring recommended.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain crop rotation, balanced irrigation, and nutrient management.

Wheat___Brown_rust.symptoms: Orange-brown oval pustules scattered on leaf surface. Yellow halo around pustules. Heavy infection causes leaves to dry out.
Wheat___Brown_rust.organic_treatment: Plant resistant varieties. Early sowing to avoid peak rust season. Remove volunteer wheat plants.
Wheat___Brown_rust.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L. Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L. Apply at first sign of disease.
Wheat___Brown_rust.prevention: Use certified rust-resistant seed varieties. Timely sowing. Balanced potassium application.
Wheat___Brown_rust.economic_impact: 10–40% yield loss; very high in epidemic years

Wheat___Yellow_rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in stripes along leaf veins. Severely infected fields appear yellow.
Wheat___Yellow_rust.favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (2–15°C), high humidity, prolonged leaf wetness
Wheat___Yellow_rust.organic_treatment: Early sowing to escape peak season. Resistant varieties. Field scouting from tillering stage.
Wheat___Yellow_rust.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole @ 1ml/L at first sign. Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole @ 1ml/L. Apply twice, 15 days apart.
Wheat___Yellow_rust.prevention: Grow resistant/tolerant varieties. Avoid late sowing in stripe-rust-prone areas.
Wheat___Yellow_rust.economic_impact: Up to 70% yield loss in susceptible varieties during epidemic years

Rice___Blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centre and brown border on leaves. Node blast causes entire panicle to collapse (neck blast).
Rice___Blast.favorable_conditions: High humidity (>90%), cool nights (24–28°C day / below 20°C night), high nitrogen
Rice___Blast.organic_treatment: Silicon fertilization (improves resistance). Trichoderma seed treatment. Avoid excess nitrogen.
Rice___Blast.chemical_treatment: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L. Isoprothiolane @ 1.5ml/L. Carbendazim @ 1g/L. Apply at booting stage.
Rice___Blast.prevention: Use blast-resistant varieties. Balanced nitrogen application. Avoid water stress at booting.
Rice___Blast.economic_impact: Can cause 100% panicle loss (neck blast) in severe cases

Rice___Brown_spot.symptoms: Brown oval spots with yellow halo on leaves. Grains show dark brown discolouration. Seedling blight (dirty panicle).
Rice___Brown_spot.favorable_conditions: High humidity, temperature 25–30°C, potassium deficiency, drought stress
Rice___Brown_spot.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg. Potassium application to stressed crops.
Rice___Brown_spot.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L. Iprodione @ 1.5ml/L. Apply at tillering and panicle initiation.
Rice___Brown_spot.prevention: Use certified healthy seed. Adequate potassium fertilization. Avoid water stress.

Cotton___Bacterial_blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked lesions on leaves bounded by veins. Lesions turn brown. Stem cankers. Boll rot.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. malvacearum
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm (27–30°C), wet conditions during boll formation, wounds from insects
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.organic_treatment: Use disease-free certified seed. Remove and destroy infected plant debris. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3g/L. Streptomycin sulfate + Copper oxychloride. Apply 3 sprays at 15-day intervals.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties. Seed treatment with hot water. Crop rotation.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown angular spots with concentric rings on lower leaves. Yellow halo. Progresses upward.
Potato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm days, cool nights, high humidity, nitrogen stress
Potato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Neem-based sprays. Compost to improve plant health. Remove infected foliage.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb @ 2.5g/L. Chlorothalonil @ 2g/L. Apply every 7–10 days from 30 days after planting.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Certified seed tubers. Crop rotation. Proper fertilization.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves turning dark brown. White sporulation on undersides. Stem lesions. Tuber rot.
Potato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Temperature 10–25°C, rainfall, >90% humidity for 2+ consecutive days
Potato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (1%). Remove and destroy infected haulms. Improve field drainage.
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb @ 2.5g/L. Cymoxanil @ 1g/L. Dimethomorph @ 1g/L. Alternate fungicides to prevent resistance.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Certified seed. Resistant varieties. Avoid planting in low-lying waterlogged areas. Hilling.
Potato___Late_blight.economic_impact: 50–100% crop loss possible; potato famine history

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular lesions on leaves with black pycnidia. Berries turn brown then black and shrivel (mummies).
Grape___Black_rot.favorable_conditions: Warm wet weather (20–30°C) during flowering and berry development
Grape___Black_rot.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy mummified berries. Prune for air circulation. Copper fungicide at bud break.
Grape___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb @ 2g/L. Myclobutanil @ 0.5ml/L. Azoxystrobin @ 1ml/L. Apply from bud break to veraison.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummies. Train vines for air circulation. Avoid wetting foliage.
Grape___Black_rot.economic_impact: Complete berry loss in severe outbreaks

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown oval pustules on both leaf surfaces. Later pustules turn dark (teliospores). Severe infection causes leaf death.
Corn___Common_rust.favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (16–23°C), high humidity, heavy dew
Corn___Common_rust.organic_treatment: Plant resistant hybrids. Remove severely infected leaves. Good field sanitation.
Corn___Common_rust.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole @ 1ml/L. Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole @ 1ml/L. Apply at VT (tasseling) stage.
Corn___Common_rust.prevention: Use resistant hybrids. Avoid late planting in rust-prone areas.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Large (5–15cm) cigar-shaped tan-grey lesions on leaves. Lesions coalesce causing complete leaf death in severe cases.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures (18–27°C), prolonged leaf wetness, high humidity
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_treatment: Crop rotation. Tillage to bury residue. Resistant hybrids.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.chemical_treatment: Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole @ 1ml/L. Apply at VT/R1 stage when disease first appears.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Resistant hybrids. Avoid monocropping. Residue management.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.economic_impact: 20–50% yield loss; higher in wet seasons

Anthracnose.symptoms: Dark sunken lesions on fruit, leaves, and stems. Fruit rot in storage. Black spots on leaves with yellow halo.
Anthracnose.favorable_conditions: Warm humid conditions (25–30°C), rain splash, high humidity
Anthracnose.organic_treatment: Remove infected plant parts. Copper-based sprays (Bordeaux mixture). Hot water seed treatment. Neem oil sprays.
Anthracnose.prevention: Use disease-free planting material. Avoid overhead irrigation. Good orchard sanitation.
Anthracnose.economic_impact: 30–70% post-harvest fruit loss; severe quality degradation

Bacterial Canker.symptoms: Water-soaked angular lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit. Cankers on bark. Gum exudation. Wilting of young shoots.
Bacterial Canker.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas campestris / X. citri
Bacterial Canker.favorable_conditions: Warm wet weather, wounds from insects or hail, high nitrogen
Bacterial Canker.organic_treatment: Prune and destroy infected branches. Copper oxychloride spray. Avoid wounding plants.
Bacterial Canker.chemical_treatment: Streptomycin sulfate 90% + Tetracycline 10% @ 0.5g/L. Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3g/L.
Bacterial Canker.prevention: Use certified disease-free nursery plants. Avoid excessive nitrogen. Control insect vectors.
Bacterial Canker.economic_impact: Significant fruit and foliage loss; can kill young trees

Bacterial Leaf Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked leaf margins that turn yellow then white/straw colored. Milky bacterial ooze on cut leaf edges in morning.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae
Bacterial Leaf Blight.favorable_conditions: Flooding, high nitrogen, temperature 25–30°C, wind-driven rain
Bacterial Leaf Blight.organic_treatment: Drain field and reduce nitrogen. Use resistant varieties. Seed treatment with bleaching powder.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride @ 3g/L. Streptomycin @ 0.5g/L. Apply at tillering and booting stage.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.prevention: Resistant varieties. Balanced nitrogen. Avoid flooding. Remove ratoon stubble.
Bacterial Leaf Blight.economic_impact: 10–50% yield loss; up to 75% in severe outbreaks

BacterialBlights.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions that turn brown/black. Wilting. Stem cankers. Foul smell in some cases.
BacterialBlights.cause: Various bacterial pathogens (Xanthomonas, Pseudomonas, Erwinia species)
BacterialBlights.favorable_conditions: Warm moist conditions, wounds, high plant density
BacterialBlights.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected material. Copper-based bactericides. Improve air circulation.
BacterialBlights.prevention: Use certified seed. Crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation.
BacterialBlights.economic_impact: Variable — 20–60% yield loss depending on crop and timing

Brown Spot.symptoms: Brown oval to circular spots on leaves with yellow halo. Grain discolouration. Seedling blight.
Brown Spot.cause: Fungal pathogen Bipolaris oryzae / Helminthosporium species
Brown Spot.favorable_conditions: High humidity, potassium deficiency, drought stress, 25–30°C
Brown Spot.organic_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg. Potassium application.
Brown Spot.prevention: Use certified healthy seed. Adequate potassium fertilization. Avoid water stress.

Cassava___bacterial_blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots, wilting, stem cankers, gum exudation. Leaf blight and die-back.
Cassava___bacterial_blight.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis
Cassava___bacterial_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm humid conditions, rainy season, wounds
Cassava___bacterial_blight.organic_treatment: Use disease-free cuttings. Remove infected plants. Copper-based bactericides.
Cassava___bacterial_blight.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride @ 3g/L. Apply at first signs of disease.
Cassava___bacterial_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free cuttings. Rogue out infected plants. Crop rotation.

Cassava___brown_streak_disease.symptoms: Yellow-green chlorotic patches on leaves. Brown streaking on stems. Root necrosis (brown rot inside tubers).
Cassava___brown_streak_disease.cause: Cassava brown streak virus (CBSV) transmitted by whitefly
Cassava___brown_streak_disease.favorable_conditions: Whitefly populations, hot dry conditions, coastal lowlands
Cassava___brown_streak_disease.organic_treatment: Plant resistant/tolerant varieties. Control whitefly with yellow sticky traps and neem oil.
Cassava___brown_streak_disease.prevention: Use certified virus-free planting material. Rogue out infected plants early. Control whitefly.
Cassava___brown_streak_disease.economic_impact: Up to 100% tuber loss; renders roots inedible

Cassava___green_mottle.symptoms: Mosaic/mottle patterns on leaves. Mild leaf distortion. Reduced leaf size.
Cassava___green_mottle.favorable_conditions: Presence of vector insects, warm humid conditions
Cassava___green_mottle.organic_treatment: Use clean planting material. Remove infected plants.
Cassava___green_mottle.chemical_treatment: Control insect vectors with appropriate insecticides.
Cassava___green_mottle.prevention: Use certified virus-free cuttings. Plant resistant varieties.

Cassava___healthy.symptoms: No visible disease. Deep green leaves, vigorous growth.
Cassava___healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain good soil health and fertilization.

Cassava___mosaic_disease.symptoms: Mosaic yellowing of leaves. Leaf distortion and twisting. Stunted plant growth. Severe yield reduction.
Cassava___mosaic_disease.cause: African cassava mosaic virus (ACMV) and related begomoviruses, transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci
Cassava___mosaic_disease.favorable_conditions: High whitefly populations, dry season, stressed plants
Cassava___mosaic_disease.organic_treatment: Use CMD-resistant varieties. Rogue out infected plants at early stage. Control whitefly with neem oil.
Cassava___mosaic_disease.chemical_treatment: Imidacloprid @ 0.5ml/L for whitefly. Thiamethoxam seed treatment.
Cassava___mosaic_disease.prevention: Plant CMD-resistant certified varieties. Use whitefly-free cuttings. Field monitoring.
Cassava___mosaic_disease.economic_impact: 30–100% yield loss — most devastating cassava disease in Africa and South Asia

Cutting Weevil.symptoms: Wilting of young shoots. Tunnelling damage in stem cuttings. Dead hearts in young plants.
Cutting Weevil.favorable_conditions: Dry season, stressed cuttings, poor storage
Cutting Weevil.organic_treatment: Treat cuttings with wood ash. Plant immediately after cutting. Use healthy stems.
Cutting Weevil.chemical_treatment: Dip cuttings in Chlorpyrifos @ 2ml/L before planting.
Cutting Weevil.prevention: Use fresh healthy cuttings. Plant at start of rainy season. Proper cutting storage.

Die Back.symptoms: Drying and death of twigs from tip downwards. Brown discolouration of wood. Bark cracking. Gum exudation.
Die Back.cause: Fungal pathogens Botryodiplodia theobromae / Lasiodiplodia theobromae
Die Back.favorable_conditions: Drought stress, wounding, hot dry winds, micronutrient deficiency
Die Back.organic_treatment: Prune affected parts 15cm below infected tissue. Apply Bordeaux paste on cut ends. Improve irrigation.
Die Back.chemical_treatment: Carbendazim @ 1g/L spray on cut wounds. Copper oxychloride paste on pruning cuts.
Die Back.prevention: Avoid drought stress. Balanced fertilization (especially Zinc, Boron). Proper pruning.
Die Back.economic_impact: Significant tree loss and reduced yield in orchards

Early_Blight.symptoms: Dark brown concentric ring spots (bull's-eye) on older leaves. Yellow halo. Lesions on stem and fruit.
Early_Blight.favorable_conditions: Warm days (24–29°C), cool nights, high humidity
Early_Blight.organic_treatment: Neem oil @ 3ml/L weekly. Remove infected leaves. Compost tea spray.
Early_Blight.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L. Chlorothalonil @ 2g/L. Apply every 7–10 days.
Early_Blight.prevention: Crop rotation. Stake plants. Avoid overhead watering. Disease-free seeds.

Gall Midge.symptoms: Small raised galls on leaves, petioles, and flowers. Leaf curling. Distorted growth. Premature flower/fruit drop.
Gall Midge.favorable_conditions: Cool humid conditions during flush/flowering, February–April in India
Gall Midge.organic_treatment: Collect and destroy fallen leaves with galls. Neem oil spray @ 5ml/L. Light traps.
Gall Midge.chemical_treatment: Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1ml/L. Imidacloprid @ 0.3ml/L during new flush emergence.
Gall Midge.prevention: Sanitation — collect and burn fallen infested leaves. Apply spray at new flush stage.

Healthy Rice Leaf.symptoms: No disease symptoms. Vibrant green leaves, strong tillers.
Healthy Rice Leaf.organic_treatment: Continue good agronomic practices. Regular monitoring.

Late_Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked grey-green lesions turning brown. White mold on undersides in humid conditions. Rapid plant death.
Late_Blight.favorable_conditions: Cool wet weather (10–20°C), foggy conditions, high humidity
Late_Blight.organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (1%). Remove affected plants immediately. Improve drainage.
Late_Blight.chemical_treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb @ 2.5g/L. Cymoxanil @ 1g/L. Apply every 5–7 days during outbreaks.
Late_Blight.prevention: Resistant varieties. Destroy infected debris. Avoid excessive nitrogen.
Late_Blight.economic_impact: Can cause complete crop loss within 2 weeks if unchecked

Leaf Blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centre and brown border on leaves. Rapid spread under humid conditions.
Leaf Blast.favorable_conditions: High humidity (>90%), cool nights, high nitrogen fertilization
Leaf Blast.organic_treatment: Silicon fertilization. Trichoderma seed treatment. Reduce nitrogen.
Leaf Blast.prevention: Blast-resistant varieties. Balanced nitrogen. Avoid water stress at booting.
Leaf Blast.economic_impact: Complete leaf death in severe cases; significant yield loss

Leaf scald.symptoms: Reddish-brown lesions with wavy margins on leaf tips and edges. Lesions have darker border. Leaf tip dieback.
Leaf scald.favorable_conditions: Warm humid weather, high nitrogen, lodging conditions
Leaf scald.organic_treatment: Balanced nutrition. Avoid excess nitrogen. Improve drainage.
Leaf scald.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole @ 1ml/L. Tebuconazole @ 1ml/L. Apply at tillering stage.
Leaf scald.prevention: Balanced fertilization. Plant resistant varieties. Proper plant spacing.
Leaf scald.economic_impact: 5–20% yield loss; mainly affects grain quality

Mosaic.symptoms: Yellow-green mosaic pattern on leaves. Leaf distortion. Stunted growth. Reduced fruit size.
Mosaic.cause: Various mosaic viruses transmitted by aphids, whiteflies, or mechanical contact
Mosaic.organic_treatment: Remove infected plants immediately. Control vector insects with neem oil. Use reflective mulch to deter aphids.
Mosaic.prevention: Use certified virus-free seed. Resistant varieties. Control insect vectors.
Mosaic.economic_impact: 30–80% yield loss; no cure once infected

Narrow Brown Leaf Spot.symptoms: Narrow linear brown spots on leaves parallel to leaf margins. Spots have dark brown border.
Narrow Brown Leaf Spot.favorable_conditions: High humidity, silicon deficiency, dense plantings
Narrow Brown Leaf Spot.organic_treatment: Silicon fertilization (improves resistance). Balanced nutrition. Proper spacing.
Narrow Brown Leaf Spot.prevention: Silicon application. Avoid dense planting. Use resistant varieties.

Neck_Blast.symptoms: Brown lesion at neck of panicle. Entire panicle turns white/grey (dead neck). Complete grain failure.
Neck_Blast.favorable_conditions: High humidity during booting/heading, cool temperatures, high nitrogen
Neck_Blast.organic_treatment: Silicon fertilization. Avoid excess nitrogen at panicle initiation.
Neck_Blast.chemical_treatment: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L at booting stage. Repeat 7–10 days later.
Neck_Blast.prevention: Resistant varieties. Apply fungicide at booting. Balanced nitrogen.
Neck_Blast.economic_impact: Can cause 100% panicle loss — most devastating rice disease

Powdery Mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaf surface and stems. Affected leaves turn yellow and dry. Stunted growth.
Powdery Mildew.cause: Fungal pathogens Erysiphe / Blumeria / Podosphaera species (obligate parasites)
Powdery Mildew.favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures (18–25°C), high humidity, poor air circulation, shade
Powdery Mildew.organic_treatment: Neem oil @ 5ml/L. Baking soda solution (5g/L). Remove infected plant parts.
Powdery Mildew.chemical_treatment: Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 1ml/L. Tebuconazole @ 1ml/L. Sulfur dust @ 25 kg/ha.
Powdery Mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Proper plant spacing for air flow. Avoid excess nitrogen.
Powdery Mildew.economic_impact: 10–30% yield loss; severe in wheat during cool humid periods

RedRot.symptoms: Reddish discolouration inside stalk with white patches (intermittent red and white). Sour/alcoholic smell. Wilting.
RedRot.favorable_conditions: Warm humid conditions (28–32°C), waterlogging, wounds from borers
RedRot.organic_treatment: Treat setts with Carbendazim @ 1g/L for 30 min before planting. Remove and burn infected clumps.
RedRot.chemical_treatment: Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L sett treatment. Propiconazole soil drench in early cases.
RedRot.prevention: Use disease-free certified setts. Resistant varieties. Control stalk borers.
RedRot.economic_impact: 20–50% cane yield loss; major quality loss (reduced sugar recovery)

Rice Hispa.symptoms: White streaks on leaves (larval mining). Scraping of upper leaf surface. Defoliation in severe cases.
Rice Hispa.favorable_conditions: High humidity, dense plantings, early planted crops, July–September
Rice Hispa.organic_treatment: Clip and destroy infested leaf tips. Manual collection. Neem oil spray @ 5ml/L.
Rice Hispa.chemical_treatment: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 1.5ml/L. Quinalphos @ 1.5ml/L. Apply at 2–3 adults/hill.
Rice Hispa.prevention: Avoid dense planting. Use light traps. Clip infested leaf tips at transplanting.

Rust.symptoms: Orange-brown or yellow powdery pustules on leaf surfaces. Leaves yellow and die. Stem weakening in severe cases.
Rust.favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures (15–22°C), leaf wetness, dew
Rust.organic_treatment: Plant resistant varieties. Potassium application (improves resistance). Remove volunteer plants.
Rust.chemical_treatment: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L. Tebuconazole @ 1ml/L. Apply at first sign of disease.
Rust.prevention: Resistant varieties. Timely sowing. Balanced potassium fertilization.
Rust.economic_impact: 10–70% yield loss depending on crop and epidemic severity

Sheath Blight.symptoms: Oval/elliptical lesions with green-grey centre and brown border on leaf sheath. Lesions coalesce. Lodging.
Sheath Blight.favorable_conditions: High humidity, temperatures 28–32°C, dense plantings, high nitrogen
Sheath Blight.organic_treatment: Reduce nitrogen. Proper plant spacing. Trichoderma viride soil application.
Sheath Blight.prevention: Resistant varieties. Balanced nitrogen. Wide spacing. Drain field periodically.
Sheath Blight.economic_impact: 10–30% yield loss; one of the most widespread rice diseases in India

Sooty Mould.symptoms: Black sooty coating on leaves and fruit surface. Reduces photosynthesis. Associated with insect (scale, mealybug) infestations.
Sooty Mould.cause: Fungal pathogens Capnodium, Meliola species — grow on honeydew secreted by insects
Sooty Mould.favorable_conditions: Presence of sap-sucking insects (scales, mealybugs, aphids, whiteflies), high humidity
Sooty Mould.organic_treatment: Control the insect causing honeydew. Wash leaves with soap water. Neem oil spray.
Sooty Mould.chemical_treatment: Imidacloprid @ 0.5ml/L to control insects. Copper oxychloride @ 3g/L for mould.
Sooty Mould.prevention: Control honeydew-producing insects. Prune for air circulation.
Sooty Mould.economic_impact: Reduces fruit quality and market value; indirect — depends on insect pressure

Yellow.symptoms: Midrib of leaves turns yellow (lemon yellow). Yellowing progresses from tip to base. Reduced tillering and stalk growth.
Yellow.cause: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) transmitted by aphid Melanaphis sacchari
Yellow.favorable_conditions: High aphid populations, ratoon crops, warm humid conditions
Yellow.organic_treatment: Remove infected stools. Use disease-free setts. Control aphid vectors with neem oil.
Yellow.chemical_treatment: Imidacloprid @ 0.5ml/L to control aphid vector. Apply at 30 and 60 days after planting.
Yellow.prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material. Control aphids. Avoid ratoon of infected crop.
Yellow.economic_impact: 20–40% sucrose content reduction; significant mill revenue loss

healthy_mango_leaf.symptoms: No disease symptoms. Glossy dark green leaves, normal growth.
healthy_mango_leaf.organic_treatment: Continue regular monitoring and good orchard management.
healthy_mango_leaf.prevention: Maintain soil health, irrigation, and balanced fertilization.

healthy_potato_leaf.symptoms: No disease symptoms. Dark green leaves, strong stems.
healthy_potato_leaf.prevention: Crop rotation, certified seed tubers, balanced fertilization.

healthy_sugarcane_leaf.symptoms: No disease symptoms. Upright green canes, normal growth.
healthy_sugarcane_leaf.organic_treatment: Maintain regular irrigation and fertilization schedule.
healthy_sugarcane_leaf.prevention: Balanced nutrition, certified setts, regular monitoring.

Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark brown with yellow halo. Fruit develops raised scabby lesions. Defoliation.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.favorable_conditions: Warm (24–30°C), wet conditions, rain splash, wounds
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Copper-based bactericide (Bordeaux mixture). Remove infected leaves. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride @ 3g/L. Streptomycin @ 0.5g/L. Apply every 7–10 days.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed. Crop rotation. Resistant varieties.

Pepper__bell___healthy.symptoms: No disease. Deep green leaves, firm fruit.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark brown water-soaked spots on leaves, stems, and fruit. Yellow halo around spots. Defoliation. Fruit blemishes.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas perforans / X. euvesicatoria
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.favorable_conditions: Warm (24–30°C), wet conditions, rain splash, wounds
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Copper bactericide sprays. Remove infected leaves. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper oxychloride @ 3g/L. Streptomycin + Copper oxychloride mixture.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Certified seed. Crop rotation. Resistant varieties.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface. Olive-green to grey-brown velvety mold on lower surface. Leaves curl and drop.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.favorable_conditions: High humidity (>85%), poor air circulation, temperature 22–25°C, greenhouse conditions
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.organic_treatment: Improve ventilation. Reduce humidity. Neem oil spray @ 3ml/L.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Resistant varieties. Proper ventilation in greenhouses. Avoid leaf wetness.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark brown border and grey/white centre on lower leaves. Black pycnidia in centre. Rapid defoliation.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.favorable_conditions: Warm (20–25°C), wet weather, leaf wetness, dense plantings
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves. Avoid overhead irrigation. Copper sprays.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Crop rotation. Avoid wetting foliage. Use mulch to prevent soil splash.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.economic_impact: Complete defoliation possible if untreated; 30–50% yield loss

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on upper leaf surface. Webbing on leaves and stems. Bronze/brown leaves. Defoliation in severe cases.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.favorable_conditions: Hot dry conditions (>28°C), low humidity, dusty conditions, drought stress
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.organic_treatment: Neem oil @ 5ml/L. Spray water on undersides of leaves. Release predatory mite Phytoseiulus persimilis.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.chemical_treatment: Abamectin 1.9% EC @ 0.5ml/L. Spiromesifen @ 1ml/L. Alternate miticides to prevent resistance.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.prevention: Maintain adequate moisture. Avoid dusty conditions. Monitor with 10x lens.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.economic_impact: 20–50% yield loss; severe in hot dry seasons

Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Dark brown concentric ring lesions with yellow halo on leaves and fruit. Similar to early blight but more circular.
Tomato__Target_Spot.favorable_conditions: Warm (22–28°C), wet conditions, high humidity, dense canopy
Tomato__Target_Spot.organic_treatment: Remove infected leaves. Improve air circulation. Copper-based sprays.
Tomato__Target_Spot.prevention: Stake plants for air flow. Crop rotation. Avoid dense plantings.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaves. Stunted growth. Flower drop. Severely reduced fruit set.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.cause: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.favorable_conditions: High whitefly populations, hot dry conditions, summer months
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.organic_treatment: Remove infected plants immediately. Yellow sticky traps. Reflective mulch. Neem oil for whitefly.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.prevention: TYLCV-resistant varieties. Whitefly-proof netting. Remove infected plants early.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.economic_impact: Near total crop loss if infection is early in the season

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic (light and dark green) pattern on leaves. Leaf distortion. Stunted growth. Reduced and malformed fruit.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV) — highly contagious, spread by contact and seed
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.favorable_conditions: Mechanical contact during pruning/transplanting, infected seed, aphid vectors
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_treatment: Remove infected plants. Disinfect tools with bleach. Plant resistant varieties.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.chemical_treatment: No cure — focus on prevention and vector control (aphids).
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Certified virus-free seed. Resistant varieties. Wash hands and disinfect tools.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.economic_impact: 30–70% yield loss; no effective chemical cure

Tomato_healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms. Deep green leaves, firm red/green fruit.

general_advice.when_to_consult: Contact your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agriculture officer if disease spreads to >30% of crop area.
general_advice.ipm_principle: Integrated Pest Management (IPM): prefer cultural and biological controls first, use chemicals only when economic threshold is exceeded.
general_advice.resistance_management: Rotate fungicides with different modes of action to prevent resistance development.
general_advice.safe_handling: Always wear protective equipment when applying pesticides. Follow label directions. Observe pre-harvest intervals (PHI).
